title: an ssh session CC started classes as cc
intention: A process that CC started over ssh classes as cc at the artifact door, so the journal, the question door and approve read an LLM's hand as an LLM's, never as Akien's.
why: Measured 2026-11-16 on akiendelllinux: caller() classes every logind session-*.scope as akien, and akienasus's CC works here over ssh in such scopes. So 1002 commons journal entries and 669 cairn journal entries whose ancestry runs through ssh.service are classed akien, cairn question answer recorded open-623b3822d036 and open-cddc9e378ee6 as 'recorded by caller class akien', and artifact.approve, which admits only the akien class, would admit CC. No physical signal separates CC-over-ssh from Akien-over-ssh today.
traces_to: Law 7: the journal is a record of truth and records CC's writes as Akien's. Outline 17.2.1: the one writer question is LLM or code. Law 6: approve is Akien's gate.
how: caller() in cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py walks the ancestry for an sshd-session process; for one, it reads that pid's 'Accepted publickey ... SHA256:<fp>' line (journalctl -u ssh _PID=<pid>, readable by the adm group, measured 2026-11-18) and classes the caller cc when <fp> is listed in cairn/tools/artifact/cc_ssh_keys.json. A red-first proof pins it over a scratch ancestry and a stubbed journal read.

out: the journal entries already written (hash-chained, append-only)

measured.saw: three live logind sessions session-2609, 2620 and 2667.scope, Service=sshd, RemoteHost=10.0.0.68 (akienasus), running bash under CC's scratchpad /tmp/claude-1000/...546bccde.../scratchpad; their environment carries SSH_CONNECTION but no CAIRN_USER and no CLAUDECODE
measured.how: loginctl show-session, and /proc/<pid>/environ for each pid in the scopes' cgroup.procs

measured.saw: every accepted login from 10.0.0.68 in the last 12 h used ED25519 SHA256:rn8eUJ+1AcWvRxs/2LHiRHhPb2sow+Z2PX7U+ci1MP8, which is the authorized key 'akien@akienasus', the same key Akien's own ssh from akienasus uses; sshd AcceptEnv is LANG LC_* COLORTERM NO_COLOR and PermitUserEnvironment is no

entries classed akien with ssh.service in their ancestry: CairnCommons journal 1002 (cast 341, append 519, outline_check 94, question 28, answer 15, phase 5), cairn journal 669 (seal 663, append 6); approvals (entries carrying approved_by_words) in either journal: 0, so CC on akienasus has never approved over ssh, nor has anyone approved at all
measured.how: a read-only scan of both house journals' caller.ancestry and approved_by_words

measured.saw: akienasus's own correction lines in commons f247efb2 are classed akien from session-2685.scope, whose ancestry ends in 1729:ssh.service, so every Dell crossing akienasus makes over ssh is journaled as Akien
measured.how: akienasus's measurement, relayed by the orchestrator

measured.saw: cairn question answer recorded open-623b3822d036 and open-cddc9e378ee6 as 'recorded by caller class akien' though CC answered over ssh
measured.how: the orchestrator's measurement of the two question records

measured.saw: consumers of caller(): the journal entry (artifact.py:602) and relanded_by, parked_by and refused.by; question.py raised_by (:171), answered_by (:240) and the migration (:291); artifact.approve (:1190, akien only); trouble.py:307 (an operator-class hand closes a trouble); diagnostic.py:443; bus server shutdown (server.py:695). No PROVED certificate carries a caller, and sail's asked_by is a stated 'CC'
measured.how: git grep on origin/main for caller() and its class reads

measured.saw: each accepted login logs 'sshd-session[PID]: Accepted publickey for akien from <ip> ... ED25519 SHA256:<fp>', and akien is in adm, so the journal line is readable without a host change

outcomes.claim: a caller whose ancestry holds an sshd-session process whose accepted key fingerprint (its 'Accepted publickey' journal line, matched by that pid) is listed in cairn/tools/artifact/cc_ssh_keys.json classes cc, and artifact.approve refuses it
the same ancestry whose accepted key is not listed classes akien, and a local app-*.scope or sddm session-*.scope with no sshd-session ancestor still classes akien
a journal entry and a question answer written by the caller of outcome 1 both name class cc

constraints: caller() decides from the kernel's record and sshd's journal, never from an environment variable: the key is the signal (outline 17.2.2).

cairn/tools/artifact/cc_ssh_keys.json lists public key fingerprints only, one {box, fingerprint} per CC key; its consumers (the journal entry, question.py, artifact.approve, the trouble operator close) read caller() unchanged.
a journal that cannot be read leaves the class as the cgroup says and records why on the caller record (Law 7); it never guesses cc or akien.
the proof pins caller() over a scratch ancestry and a scratch journal reader, as cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_the_caller_reads_whose_terminal_it_is.py does; no live sshd is touched.

out of this ticket: making CC's key on each box and pointing CC's ssh at it (a host-seam of its own), the interim refusal of every sshd-session caller at approve and the operator close (its own ticket, sailing first), and the claude_code user per box (outline 17.2.2.1, a later intention).
